blocks.text: More Burnaby real estate
Condo buildings in Central Park
Central Park House — 5987 Wilson Avenue

A 41-storey residential high-rise by Bosa Properties, built in 2025 per current listings, designed by Gensler Architects, steps to Patterson SkyTrain Station and Central Park. Listings describe 24/7 concierge, an indoor pool and hot tub on the 17th floor, a 2,000 sq ft fitness centre, sauna and steam rooms, co-work space and social lounge, with 1 parking and 1 locker for the units checked. Published positions in listing fields include pets: a rental listing for the building calls it pet-friendly, and one sale listing records "Pets Allowed With Restrictions" — registered bylaws govern.
Paramount II — 5899 Wilson Avenue

A concrete high-rise by Bosa, built in 1996 per current listings, described as a 134-unit development in a building directory's listing record ("134 Unit Development, Concrete"), just minutes to Patterson and Metrotown stations and across from Central Park. The same directory record is titled "Pets Allowed" for this building. One listing notes the neighbouring Paramount (5833 Wilson) has an updated envelope "unlike 5899 Wilson".
Paramount — 5833 Wilson Avenue

A concrete building by Bosa in the heart of Metrotown, according to current listings, with an exercise centre, steam room and bike room. Listings give 1994 as the year built, while a building directory and another listing say 1995.
Aldynne on the Park — 5883 Barker Avenue

A concrete tower by Polygon, built in 2017 per current listings, directly across from Central Park and minutes to Patterson SkyTrain Station, with a fitness centre and lounge. A building directory records its strata bylaws as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. (One older building page gives a different build year (2014) and a different street address for this name; the 2017 / 5883 Barker Avenue position is the one current listings and the building directory agree on, and the older page is not relied on.)
Central Park Place — 5652 Patterson Avenue

A listing for a home at this address calls it "Central Park Place", a concrete building, with 2 parking stalls and 1 locker for that home, and gives 1981 as the year built. A rental website's building profile gives the same name and address as 408 units, 21 storeys, built in 1992.
Central Park Place — 4160 Sardis Street

A separate building carrying the same name, on Sardis Street north of the park: a building directory records it as built in 1977, with an exercise centre, outdoor pool, recreation centre, sauna/steam room, swirlpool/hot tub and tennis courts, and records its strata bylaws as: pets not allowed, rentals not allowed — the "rentals not allowed" line is void: strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 (Bill 44). The pets-not-allowed line is a pet bylaw, which remains enforceable — confirm both on the Form B.
Grand Central Park Place — 6128 Patterson Avenue
A building directory records Grand Central Park Place at this address, built in 1992.

items.t: The Central Park sub-area is the residential area around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, on the Vancouver border at Kingsway, directly west of Metrotown. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the residential area surrounds the park, between Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) and Metrotown, along Kingsway and Imperial Street. Heritage Burnaby describes the park itself as lying between 49th Avenue to the south, Kingsway to the north, Boundary Road to the west and Patterson Avenue to the east.

Where the condos are: east of the park, on Wilson Avenue, Barker Avenue and Patterson Avenue between the park and Metrotown. There's a group of 1990s Bosa concrete buildings (Paramount, Paramount II, Place Meridian), a 1970s–1990s group around Patterson and Sardis (Central Park Place at two addresses, Grand Central Park Place, Wimbledon Club), one 2017 tower (Aldynne on the Park), and the area's newest tower, Central Park House (2025), at the Patterson Station end of Wilson Avenue. The streets north and south of the park itself are detached houses.

Main streets: Kingsway runs along the park's north side and Imperial Street along the south; Boundary Road is the west edge at the City of Vancouver border and Patterson Avenue is on the east side of the park. The towers are on Wilson Avenue, Barker Avenue and Sardis Street.
Transit: Patterson Station (Expo Line) is at the park's north-east corner and Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is east of the park.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Park condos

items.t: One name, three buildings, two tenures of use. "Central Park Place" is a 1977 residential building at 4160 Sardis Street, a residential building at 5652 Patterson Avenue whose build year sources dispute (1981 vs 1992), and an 18-storey Bosa office tower at 4555 Kingsway built in 2000. Any search, document order or depreciation-report request made on the name alone can land on the wrong corporation.

The park's edges are heritage-recorded, and they fix the sub-area's shape. Heritage Burnaby records Central Park's ceremonial entrance gate on Kingsway (associated dates 1913) and the Jubilee Grove Arch at Kingsway and Patterson Avenue (1939), and describes the park as lying between 49th Avenue, Kingsway, Boundary Road and Patterson Avenue — the same four edges the condo grid sits outside of, east of Patterson.

A neighbouring building's listing compares itself with this one. A Paramount (5833 Wilson) listing says its building has an "UPDATED ENVELOPE unlike 5899 Wilson". That's a seller's claim; read both buildings' depreciation reports.

The BC Parkway trail runs through Central Park under the elevated Expo Line. The walk from Patterson to Metrotown that tower listings call "steps to the park" is a lit, paved path. For every building except those at the Patterson corner, getting to SkyTrain means that walk; the station isn't at the door.

French Immersion sits inside the catchment conversation here. Listings that present Inman as "the school" for a Wilson or Patterson address overstate it; the catchment elementary named in tower listings here is Chaffey-Burke.

items.t: "Central Park" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name: the residential area around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, from Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) to Metrotown, between Kingsway, Imperial Street and the park. Central Park itself is bounded by 49th Avenue, Kingsway, Boundary Road and Patterson Avenue.
Transit anchors: Patterson Station at the park's north-east corner and Metrotown Station, both Expo Line.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Park BS

items.t: Three buildings here have almost the same name: Central Park House (5987 Wilson, 2025), Central Park Place (5652 Patterson, and another at 4160 Sardis) and Grand Central Park Place (6128 Patterson), plus a Central Park office tower at 4555 Kingsway that isn't housing. It's easy to order a Form B for the wrong building, so use the address, not the name.

Listing copy for the sub-area describes Central Park as a 222-acre park — the park is the reason the Wilson/Patterson towers market "parkside" living, and its formal bounds (49th Ave / Kingsway / Boundary / Patterson) put the park itself in nobody's strata.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Park
Fee-simple lots

items.t: The only sourced lot figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: a minimum lot area of 281 m² and a minimum lot width of 10 m, with the 280 m² / 281 m² unit-count thresholds. These are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Servicing, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Parcel-level servicing for a specific lot: confirm with the City.
Parcel-level ALR status is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

blocks.text: Named developments / applications

items.t: I don't know of any bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Central Park

Plans that apply to any future proposal: Metrotown is Burnaby's downtown under the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, and the City allows higher-density housing, including towers, walk-ups and townhouses, in the town centres. The 2050 plan overrides older community plan maps where they conflict, so check the assembly value of a lot on Kingsway or Imperial against the 2050 plan and the Metrotown plan, not an older map.

items.t: Nearby: Metrotown to the east, South Slope and Garden Village to the southeast, the separate "Central" area (Canada Way and Deer Lake) to the northeast, and Vancouver across Boundary Road to the west.

Roads and transit: Kingsway runs along the park's north side and Imperial Street along the south, with Boundary Road on the west edge at the Vancouver border and Patterson Avenue on the east side of the park. Patterson Station is at the park's northeast corner and Metrotown Station is east of the park, both on the Expo Line.

Parks, recreation, library, health: Central Park itself is the sub-area's centre — the large City park on the Vancouver border at Kingsway, with the BC Parkway trail running through it under the SkyTrain line. Bonsor Recreation Complex, in the Metrotown area east of the park, serves this side of the city. The library branch serving this area is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, 6100 Willingdon Ave, east of the park. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health); the Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 102-4555 Kingsway, east of the park.

items.t: If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha).

items.t: Downtown Burnaby is next door: Central Park has no neighbourhood plan of its own. It's planned as part of the Metrotown town centre, Burnaby's downtown, directly east of the park. A lot's long-term value here depends on what happens at the edge of Metrotown.

faq.a: Central Park House (5987 Wilson Avenue, Bosa, built 2025) is the newest, ahead of Aldynne on the Park (5883 Barker Avenue, Polygon, 2017). A 2025 building is inside its 2-5-10 warranty window; confirm the warranty position for the specific unit, because the 2-year and 5-year components expire before the 10-year structural component.
faq.q: Which buildings are the newest, and does warranty remain?

faq.a: Three, counting the office tower. Residential: 5652 Patterson Avenue (a listing records it built in 1981; a rental-platform profile says 1992 and 408 units — unresolved) and 4160 Sardis Street (built 1977 per the building directory, with pool, tennis courts and a pets-not-allowed bylaw on record). Commercial: the 18-storey office tower at 4555 Kingsway, built by Bosa in 2000. Always quote the street address with the name.
faq.q: Two buildings are both called Central Park Place — which is which?

faq.a: Half of it is void. The "rentals not allowed" line cannot be enforced: strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. The "pets not allowed" line is a pet bylaw, which remains enforceable in BC — so a buyer with a pet should treat 4160 Sardis as no-pets until the registered bylaws on the Form B say otherwise, while a buyer planning to rent the unit out can rely on the rental voidness.
faq.q: A directory says Central Park Place (4160 Sardis) allows no rentals and no pets — is that right?

faq.a: It varies by building: Aldynne on the Park allows pets with restrictions (directory); Paramount II (5899 Wilson) says "Pets Allowed"; Central Park House is pet friendly according to one listing, with restrictions according to another; a Wimbledon Club listing says cats are allowed; and a Place Meridian listing says no pets. Listings aren't bylaws; read the registered bylaws for the specific building.
faq.q: Are pets allowed in the other towers?

faq.a: The one detailed published record is Place Meridian (5967 Wilson Avenue): complete repiping and boiler replacement (2023), elevator modernization (2024), swimming pool rehabilitation (2024) and updated common areas (2025), per a current listing. For Paramount II, a neighbouring building's listing claims Paramount (5833 Wilson) has an updated envelope "unlike 5899 Wilson".
faq.q: What capital work has already been done in the older buildings?

faq.a: No. Central Park is the area by the park on the Vancouver border, west of Metrotown; "Central" is a separate area around Canada Way and Deer Lake to the northeast, with different homes and figures.
faq.q: Is Central Park the same as "Central"?

faq.a: No known one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering is known. The market is built houses on the park-side streets and strata product toward the stations.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Central Park?

faq.a: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m and minimum lot area 281 m² for SSMUH lots, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. With Patterson and Metrotown stations framing the area, measure the 400 m test on the actual parcel.
faq.q: How many homes can an R1 lot hold here?

faq.a: Around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, between Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) and Metrotown, along Kingsway and Imperial Street. "Central Park" is the MLS® area name, and it's part of Burnaby South.
faq.q: Where is the Central Park sub-area in Burnaby?

faq.a: Maywood Community Elementary (K–7), 4567 Imperial St, Chaffey-Burke Elementary (K–7), 4404 Sardis St, and the École Inman Elementary French Immersion program, 3963 Brandon St, with Moscrop Secondary, 4433 Moscrop St, and Burnaby South Secondary, 5455 Rumble St, the nearest secondaries; catchments are address-based — check the SD41 locator, and note French Immersion is a choice program, not a catchment.
